items.title: Euclidean spatial calculus: gradient, divergence and material derivative
items.design_state: completed-local-definition; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Throughout, $\mathbb R^3$ carries its standard ordered orthonormal basis $e_1,e_2,e_3$, its Euclidean inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_2$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $a\in O$ and let $v:O\to\mathbb R^3$ be of class $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), so that the total derivative $Dv(a):\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ is a linear map ([[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]], [[def-euclidean-linear-map]]) whose matrix in the standard bases is $\bigl(\partial_jv_i(a)\bigr)_{1\le i,j\le3}$ ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]], [[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). The **divergence** of $v$ at $a$ is

$$\operatorname{div}v(a):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(Dv(a)\bigr)=\sum_{i=1}^{3}\partial_iv_i(a),$$

the trace of the total derivative ([[def-trace-of-a-square-matrix]]), read in the standard basis of $M_3(\mathbb R)$ ([[def-matrix-space]]).

For a $C^1$ scalar field $f:O\to\mathbb R$ and $a\in O$, the **gradient** $\nabla f(a)\in\mathbb R^3$ is the vector of partial derivatives of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]; it is the unique vector with $Df(a)h=\langle\nabla f(a),h\rangle_2$ for every $h\in\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[thm-gradient-represents-directional-derivatives-and-steepest-ascent]]). We write $\langle\nabla f(a),v(a)\rangle_2=:\nabla f(a)\cdot v(a)$.

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval and let $u:I\times O\to\mathbb R^3$ and $f:I\times O\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$. For $(t,x)\in I\times O$ write $D_x f(t,x):\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ for the total derivative of $y\mapsto f(t,y)$ at fixed $t$, and $\nabla_xf(t,x)$ for its gradient. The derivative $Df(t,x)$ of the full map on $I\times O$ acts on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$; it is distinct from $D_x f$. Define the partial time derivative $\partial_tf(t,x):=\frac{d}{ds}\big|_{s=t}f(s,x)$ and the **material derivative** of $f$ along $u$

$$D_tf(t,x):=\partial_tf(t,x)+D_xf(t,x)\bigl(u(t,x)\bigr)=\partial_tf(t,x)+\nabla_x f(t,x)\cdot u(t,x).$$

Spatial derivatives $Du$, $Dw$, $\nabla f$ and $\operatorname{div}u$ of time-dependent fields always mean $D_xu$, $D_xw$, $\nabla_x f$ and spatial divergence at fixed time; a stationary field $u(x)$ is included by setting $u(t,x)=u(x)$. The same definitions apply on any open spacetime domain, by restriction to a product neighborhood of each point.

For a $C^1$ vector field $w:I\times O\to\mathbb R^3$ the material derivative $D_tw$ is defined componentwise, and $\operatorname{div}w(t,x)$ means the divergence of $x\mapsto w(t,x)$ at $x$ at each fixed $t$.

items.title: Continuum motions, spatial velocity, material acceleration and swept regions
items.design_state: completed-local-definition; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a material region (nonempty, bounded, open, [[def-cm-material-region-and-density]]) and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval ([[def-interval]]).

A **motion of $B$ on $I$** consists of an open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ with $\overline B\subseteq O$ ([[def-metric-ball]]) together with a map

$$\chi:I\times O\longrightarrow\mathbb R^3$$

such that:

1. $\chi$ is of class $C^2$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]);
2. for every $t\in I$ the map $\chi_t:=\chi(t,\cdot):O\to\mathbb R^3$ is of class $C^1$, is injective, and has $D_X\chi_t(X)$ invertible for every $X\in O$;
3. writing

$$J(t,X):=\det\bigl(D_X\chi_t(X)\bigr)$$

with the determinant of [[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]], one has $J(t,X)>0$ for every $(t,X)\in I\times B$.

We call $X\in B$ the **material label** (reference position), $x=\chi(t,X)$ the **position** at time $t$ of the label $X$, and

$$\Omega_t:=\chi_t(B)$$

the **current (material) region** at time $t$. Condition 2 makes each $\chi_t:O\to\chi_t(O)$ a $C^1$ diffeomorphism onto the open set $\chi_t(O)$ ([[cor-injective-regular-ck-map-is-a-ck-diffeomorphism-onto-its-image]]).

The **spatial velocity field** of the motion is

$$u:\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(O)\}\longrightarrow\mathbb R^3,\qquad u\bigl(t,\chi(t,X)\bigr):=\partial_t\chi(t,X),$$

and the **spatial acceleration field** is the material derivative of $u$ in the sense of [[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]],

$$a(t,x):=D_tu(t,x)=\partial_tu(t,x)+Du(t,x)u(t,x).$$

For a compact subinterval $K\subseteq I$ the **swept region** of $B$ over $K$ is

$$\Sigma_K:=\bigl\{(t,x):t\in K,\ x\in\chi_t(\overline B)\bigr\},$$

and for a scalar field $f$ on a neighbourhood of $\Sigma_K$ the spatial field $f(t,x)$ of a material quantity $F(t,X)$ is defined by $f(t,\chi(t,X))=F(t,X)$.

items.title: The derivative of the determinant along an invertible C¹ matrix curve: $(\det A)'=\det A\;\operatorname{tr}(A^{-1}A')$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, and let

$$A:I\longrightarrow M_n(\mathbb R),\qquad A(t)=\bigl(a_{ij}(t)\bigr),$$

be a matrix-valued curve whose entries $a_{ij}:I\to\mathbb R$ are differentiable at $t_0\in I$ ([[def-derivative]], [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]); write $A'(t_0):=\bigl(a_{ij}'(t_0)\bigr)$ ([[def-matrices-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Suppose $A(t)$ is invertible for every $t\in I$ ([[thm-real-square-matrix-invertible-iff-determinant-nonzero]], [[cor-inverse-matrix-by-adjugate]]). Then $t\mapsto\det A(t)$ is differentiable at $t_0$ ([[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]) and

$$(\det A)'(t_0)=\det A(t_0)\;\operatorname{tr}\!\bigl(A(t_0)^{-1}A'(t_0)\bigr),$$

with the trace of [[def-trace-of-a-square-matrix]]. In particular, a $C^1$ matrix curve with invertible values has $(\det A)'=\det A\,\operatorname{tr}(A^{-1}A')$ on all of $I$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

items.title: Localization: a continuous function whose integrals vanish over a neighbourhood-basis family is identically zero
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, which supplies the measure properties of Lebesgue measure used below ([[def-countable-choice]]).

Let $W\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $H:W\to\mathbb R$ be continuous in the Euclidean metric: for every $y\in W$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that $z\in W$, $\|z-y\|_2<\delta$ imply $|H(z)-H(y)|<\varepsilon$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a family of nonempty open subsets of $W$ such that

$$ \text{for every }y_0\in W\text{ and every neighbourhood }V\text{ of }y_0\text{ there is }A\in\mathcal F\text{ with }y_0\in A\subseteq V . \tag{L} $$

Suppose the signed Lebesgue integral is defined and $\int_AH\,dx=0$ for every $A\in\mathcal F$ ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]). Then $H=0$ on $W$.

items.title: The transport theorem for a $C^2$ family of diffeomorphisms: $\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\psi_t(B)}f=\int_{\psi_t(B)}(\partial_tf+\operatorname{div}(fw))$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the change-of-variables theorem below. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval ([[def-interval]]), let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a material region ([[def-cm-material-region-and-density]]) and let $\psi:I\times O\to\mathbb R^3$ be a motion of $B$ on $I$ in the sense of [[def-cm-continuum-motion]], with associated spatial velocity

$$w\bigl(t,\psi(t,X)\bigr)=\partial_t\psi(t,X)$$

and Jacobian $J(t,X)=\det D_X\psi_t(X)$ ([[def-cm-continuum-motion]], [[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]]).

Let $J_0\subseteq I$ be an open interval with $\overline{J_0}\subseteq I$, put

$$\Sigma:=\bigl\{(t,x):t\in\overline{J_0},\ x\in\psi_t(\overline B)\bigr\},$$

and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) on an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ containing $\Sigma$. Then

$$F(t):=\int_{\psi_t(B)}f(t,x)\,dx$$

is defined and differentiable on $J_0$ ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]), and for every $t\in J_0$

$$F'(t)=\int_{\psi_t(B)}\bigl(\partial_tf+\operatorname{div}(fw)\bigr)(t,x)\,dx,$$

with the divergence and spatial derivative of [[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]] and the Lebesgue integral of [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]. The same formula holds componentwise for $f$ replaced by a $C^1$ vector field.

references.title: R. Abeyaratne, Continuum Mechanics, Volume II of Lecture Notes on the Mechanics of Solids (MIT, 1988, revised 2020), Sections 3.7 (transport equations) and 4.2 (conservation of mass)
W. Barsukow, Introduction to Conservation Laws: Theory and Numerics (lecture notes, TUM, Winter term 2021/22), Section 1.2.3, Theorem 1.1 (the transport theorem)

items.title: Local mass balance: conservation on every material subregion implies $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the transport theorem. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a material region, let $\chi:I\times O\to\mathbb R^3$ be a motion of $B$ on $I$ with spatial velocity $u$ ([[def-cm-continuum-motion]]), and let $J_0\subseteq I$ be an open interval with $\overline{J_0}\subseteq I$. Define the swept region

$$\Sigma:=\bigl\{(t,x):t\in\overline{J_0},\ x\in\chi_t(\overline B)\bigr\}.$$

Write $\mathcal D_\chi:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(O)\}$ for the open domain of the spatial velocity $u$ ([[def-cm-continuum-motion]]). Let $U\subseteq\mathcal D_\chi$ be open and contain the swept region $\Sigma$. Let $\rho:U\to(0,\infty)$ be of class $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); call it a **density field**. A **material subregion** is a nonempty bounded open $B'\subseteq B$ with $\overline{B'}\subseteq B$ ([[def-cm-material-region-and-density]]); for such $B'$ the same $\chi$ is a motion of $B'$.

**(i) Localization.** Assume for every material subregion $B'$ and every $t\in J_0$

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho(t,x)\,dx=0, \tag{CM}$$

It is sufficient to assume this identity only for those pairs $(t,B')$ for which $\chi_t(B')$ is an open Euclidean ball with closure inside $\chi_t(B)$. Under either version of the conservation hypothesis,

$$\partial_t\rho(t,x)+\operatorname{div}\bigl(\rho u\bigr)(t,x)=0$$

for every $(t,x)\in J_0\times\chi_t(B)$, with the material derivative and divergence of [[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]].

**(ii) Converse.** Conversely, if $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0$ on an open neighbourhood of $\Sigma$ in $U$, then (CM) holds for every material subregion $B'$ and every $t\in J_0$.

references.title: R. Abeyaratne, Continuum Mechanics, Volume II of Lecture Notes on the Mechanics of Solids (MIT, 1988, revised 2020), Section 4.2 (conservation of mass and the local continuity equation)
W. Barsukow, Introduction to Conservation Laws: Theory and Numerics (lecture notes, TUM, Winter term 2021/22), Section 1.1 (integral and differential forms of the continuity equation)

items.title: Local momentum balance: $\rho D_tu=\rho b+\operatorname{div}\sigma$ from the integral balance on every material subregion
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the transport and divergence theorems. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a material region, let $\chi:I\times O\to\mathbb R^3$ be a motion of $B$ on $I$ with spatial velocity $u$ and material derivative $D_t$ ([[def-cm-continuum-motion]], [[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]]), and let $J_0\subseteq I$ be an open interval with $\overline{J_0}\subseteq I$. Define the swept region $\Sigma=\{(t,x):t\in\overline{J_0},\ x\in\chi_t(\overline B)\}$.

Write $\mathcal D_\chi:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(O)\}$ for the open domain of the spatial velocity $u$ ([[def-cm-continuum-motion]]), and take $U\subseteq\mathcal D_\chi$ open and containing $\Sigma$. Let $\rho:U\to(0,\infty)$ be a $C^1$ density field, let $\sigma:U\to M_3(\mathbb R)$ be a $C^1$ field (the stress field of [[def-cm-traction-and-stress]]), and let $b:U\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous. Suppose:

**(K)** $\rho$ satisfies $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0$ at every $(t,x)$ with $t\in J_0$ and $x\in\chi_t(B)$;

**(L)** for every material subregion $B'$ (nonempty bounded open with $\overline{B'}\subseteq B$) and every $t\in J_0$ for which $\chi_t(B')$ is a bounded $C^1$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]) , the balance is

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho(t,x)u(t,x)\,dx=\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho(t,x)b(t,x)\,dx+\int_{\partial\chi_t(B')}\sigma(t,y)\,\nu(y)\,dS(y),$$

where $\nu$ is the outward unit normal and the surface integral is that of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]].

Define the **row divergence** of $\sigma$ componentwise by

$$g(t,x):=\Bigl(\sum_{j}\partial_j\sigma_{1j},\ \sum_{j}\partial_j\sigma_{2j},\ \sum_{j}\partial_j\sigma_{3j}\Bigr)(t,x).$$

Then for every $(t,x)\in J_0\times\chi_t(B)$,

$$\rho(t,x)\,D_tu(t,x)=\rho(t,x)\,b(t,x)+g(t,x).$$

references.title: R. Abeyaratne, Continuum Mechanics, Volume II of Lecture Notes on the Mechanics of Solids (MIT, 1988, revised 2020), Sections 4.4–4.6 (balance of momentum principles and the field equations)
K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (September 1, 2026 complete volume), Section 7.2 (the stress tensor and the key equation of continuum dynamics, Eq. (7.25))

items.title: A continuous traction field balanced on every piecewise $C^1$ region is given by a continuous stress matrix, and $t(-n)=-t(n)$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ where the surface and divergence machinery of the cited items assumes it. Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $t:O\times S^2\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous, where $S^2=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:\|n\|_2=1\}$ is the unit sphere, and let $g:O\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous and bounded, with $C_g:=\sup_{O}\|g\|_2<+\infty$. Suppose that for every bounded piecewise $C^1$ Euclidean domain $D$ with a specified finite presentation ([[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]) whose closure lies in $O$ and whose associated pieces lie in $O$,

$$ \int_{\partial D}t\bigl(y,\nu_D(y)\bigr)\,dS(y)+\int_Dg(y)\,dy=0, \tag{B} $$

where $\nu_D$ is the actual outward unit normal off the edge set of the presentation, the boundary term is the sum of the surface integrals over the specified faces ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]), and values of the normal on the edge set are irrelevant.

Then there is a unique continuous map

$$\sigma:O\longrightarrow M_3(\mathbb R)$$

with

$$t(y,n)=\sigma(y)n\qquad\text{for every }(y,n)\in O\times S^2,$$

the product being matrix-vector multiplication ([[def-matrix-space]], [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]). Explicitly, the columns of $\sigma(y)$ are the vectors $t(y,e_1),t(y,e_2),t(y,e_3)$; and necessarily

$$t(y,-n)=-t(y,n)\qquad\text{for every }(y,n)\in O\times S^2 .$$

references.title: R. Abeyaratne, Continuum Mechanics, Volume II of Lecture Notes on the Mechanics of Solids (MIT, 1988, revised 2020), Section 4.3 (force, traction and Cauchy's hypothesis) and Section 4.5 (the Cauchy tetrahedron and the existence of the stress tensor)
MIT OpenCourseWare 12.005, Applications of Continuum Mechanics, Lecture 3: tensors, stress, the Cauchy tetrahedron and Cauchy's formula

items.title: Angular-momentum balance without couples forces the stress matrix to be symmetric
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the divergence and surface-integral machinery. Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $\sigma:O\to M_3(\mathbb R)$ be of class $C^1$, and let $b:O\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous. Suppose that for every bounded $C^1$ domain $D$ with $\overline D\subseteq O$ ([[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]), with outward unit normal $\nu$ and the surface integral of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]:

$$\int_{\partial D}\sigma\nu\,dS+\int_Db\,dx=0 \tag{LB}$$

and

$$\int_{\partial D}y\times(\sigma\nu)\,dS+\int_Dy\times b\,dx=0. \tag{AB}$$

Then

$$\sigma(y)^{\mathsf T}=\sigma(y)\qquad\text{for every }y\in O .$$

references.title: R. Abeyaratne, Continuum Mechanics, Volume II of Lecture Notes on the Mechanics of Solids (MIT, 1988, revised 2020), Section 4.4 (balance of angular momentum) and Section 4.5 (symmetry of the Cauchy stress tensor)
K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (September 1, 2026 complete volume), Section 7.2 (the Cauchy stress tensor; the torque argument forcing its symmetry)

items.title: Control-volume balance: mass and momentum rates for a moving non-material region
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the transport and divergence theorems. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a material region, and let $\chi:I\times O\to\mathbb R^3$ be a motion of $B$ on $I$ with spatial velocity $u$. Write

$$\mathcal D_\chi:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(O)\}$$

for the open domain on which $u$ is defined ([[def-cm-continuum-motion]]). Let $J_0\subseteq I$ be an open interval with compact closure in $I$, and let $U\subseteq\mathcal D_\chi$ be open and contain the swept region of $B$ over $\overline{J_0}$.

Let $\rho:U\to(0,\infty)$ and $\sigma:U\to M_3(\mathbb R)$ be $C^1$ and let $b:U\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous. Define $g_i:=\sum_j\partial_j\sigma_{ij}$ and suppose, on $U$:

$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0\qquad\text{and}\qquad\rho\,D_tu=\rho b+g . \tag{KM}$$

Let $\psi:I\times O'\to\mathbb R^3$ be a second motion of a material region $B'\subseteq B$ (with the same reference chart domain $O'=O$ used for $B$; write $w$ for its spatial velocity), and suppose that for every $t\in J_0$ the control region $C_t:=\psi_t(B')$ is a bounded $C^1$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]) with outward unit normal $\nu$ and boundary surface integral as in [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]].

Assume also that the control sweep $\Sigma_C:=\{(t,x):t\in\overline{J_0},\ x\in\psi_t(\overline{B'})\}$ is contained in $U$. Thus the fields and the local equations (KM) are defined on a neighbourhood of every closed control region. No condition that the control motion coincide with the material motion is imposed.

Then for every $t\in J_0$:

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{C_t}\rho\,dx=-\int_{\partial C_t}\rho\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,dS, \tag{CV1}$$

and componentwise

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{C_t}\rho u_i\,dx=\int_{C_t}\rho b_i\,dx+\Bigl(\int_{\partial C_t}\sigma\nu\,dS\Bigr)_i-\int_{\partial C_t}\rho u_i\,(u-w)\cdot\nu\,dS\qquad(i=1,2,3). \tag{CV2}$$

references.title: R. Abeyaratne, Continuum Mechanics, Volume II of Lecture Notes on the Mechanics of Solids (MIT, 1988, revised 2020), Sections 3.7 and 4.4 (transport equations for a moving part; the balance laws in integral form)

W. Barsukow, Introduction to Conservation Laws: Theory and Numerics (lecture notes, TUM, Winter term 2021/22), Sections 1.1–1.2 (Eulerian fixed-volume and Lagrangian moving-volume descriptions of the same balance)

items.title: The small-strain isotropic linear elastic constitutive law and its strain energy
items.design_state: completed-local-definition; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a material region ([[def-cm-material-region-and-density]]) and let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open with $\overline B\subseteq O$. A **displacement field** on $B$ is a map $\xi:O\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^2$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); its total derivative $D\xi(X):\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ at $X\in O$ is linear ([[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]]) and has matrix $\bigl(\partial_j\xi_i(X)\bigr)$ ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]).

Write $\operatorname{Sym}(3):=\{A\in M_3(\mathbb R):A^{\mathsf T}=A\}$ for the real symmetric $3\times3$ matrices ([[def-matrix-space]], [[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]]) and $I_3$ for the identity ([[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]). The **linear strain** of the displacement field is the symmetric-matrix field

$$e(X):=\frac{D\xi(X)+D\xi(X)^{\mathsf T}}{2}\in\operatorname{Sym}(3),\qquad e_{ij}(X)=\frac{\partial_j\xi_i(X)+\partial_i\xi_j(X)}{2},$$

the symmetric part of the Jacobian matrix, and its **trace** is $\operatorname{tr}e=\sum_i\partial_i\xi_i$ ([[def-trace-of-a-square-matrix]]). The **Frobenius inner product** of $A,C\in M_3(\mathbb R)$ is $\langle A,C\rangle_F:=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\mathsf T}C)=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}C_{ij}$, with squared norm $|A|_F^2=\langle A,A\rangle_F$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); the **deviatoric part** of $e$ is

$$e_0:=e-\frac{\operatorname{tr}e}{3}I_3 .$$

An **isotropic linear elastic constitutive law** is a pair $(\lambda,\mu)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$ of **Lamé parameters** with

$$\mu>0,\qquad \lambda+\frac{2\mu}{3}>0 .$$

Its **stress matrix field** is

$$\sigma(X):=\lambda(\operatorname{tr}e(X))I_3+2\mu\,e(X)\in\operatorname{Sym}(3),$$

and its **strain-energy density** is the real function of $e$

$$W(e):=\frac{\lambda}{2}(\operatorname{tr}e)^2+\mu\operatorname{tr}(e^2).$$

items.title: The isotropic elastic strain energy is $\mu|e_0|_F^2+(\lambda/2+\mu/3)(\operatorname{tr}e)^2$, hence positive definite under $\mu>0$, $\lambda+2\mu/3>0$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $e\in\operatorname{Sym}(3)$ with deviatoric part $e_0=e-\frac{\operatorname{tr}e}{3}I_3$ and Lamé parameters $\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb R$ with $\mu>0$ and $\lambda+\frac{2\mu}{3}>0$ ([[def-cm-linear-elastic-constitutive-law]]). Then

$$W(e)=\mu\,|e_0|_F^2+\Bigl(\frac{\lambda}{2}+\frac{\mu}{3}\Bigr)(\operatorname{tr}e)^2\ \ge\ 0,$$

and $W(e)=0$ if and only if $e=0$. Here $|A|_F^2=\operatorname{tr}(A^{\mathsf T}A)$ is the squared Frobenius norm ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-trace-of-a-square-matrix]]).

items.title: Exact plane-wave solutions of the isotropic linear elastic model, with longitudinal and transverse speeds
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $\rho_0>0$ and Lam\'e parameters $\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb R$ with $\mu>0$ and $\lambda+\frac{2\mu}{3}>0$, let $a,k\in\mathbb R^3$ and $\omega\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, and define the **plane wave**

$$\xi:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3,\qquad \xi(t,x):=a\cos\bigl(\langle k,x\rangle_2-\omega t\bigr),$$

with the Euclidean inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_2$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). For each fixed $t$, the spatial displacement map is $\xi_t(x):=\xi(t,x)$. Define the strain and stress fields using the spatial derivative at fixed time:

$$e(t,x):=\frac12\bigl(D_x\xi(t,x)+(D_x\xi(t,x))^{\mathsf T}\bigr),\qquad \sigma(t,x):=\lambda(\operatorname{tr}e(t,x))I_3+2\mu e(t,x).$$

These are the pointwise constitutive formulas of the isotropic linear elastic model ([[def-cm-linear-elastic-constitutive-law]]); in particular $D_x\xi$ is the total derivative of $x\mapsto\xi_t(x)$, not the derivative of the full spacetime map.

Then the componentwise identity

$$\rho_0\,\partial_t^2\xi_i=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\partial_j\sigma_{ij}\qquad(i=1,2,3)$$

holds on all of $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ if and only if

$$\rho_0\omega^2a=\mu|k|_2^2\,a+(\lambda+\mu)\,\langle k,a\rangle_2\,k . \tag{D}$$

When (D) holds and $a,k$ are nonzero, define the phase speed by $c_{\rm ph}:=|\omega|/|k|_2$. If $a=\alpha k$ for some $\alpha\ne0$ (**longitudinal** polarization), then $\rho_0\omega^2=(\lambda+2\mu)|k|_2^2$ and $c_{\rm ph}^2=(\lambda+2\mu)/\rho_0$. If $\langle k,a\rangle_2=0$ (**transverse** polarization), then $\rho_0\omega^2=\mu|k|_2^2$ and $c_{\rm ph}^2=\mu/\rho_0$. The constitutive positivity hypotheses imply $\lambda+2\mu=(\lambda+2\mu/3)+4\mu/3>0$ and $\mu>0$, so both branch phase speeds are real and positive. (When $k=0$, (D) has no solution with $a\ne0$ and $\omega\ne0$.)

items.title: Incompressible Newtonian and barotropic inviscid fluid constitutive models
items.design_state: completed-local-definition; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, and let $u:I\times O\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^1$ spatial velocity field with the conventions of [[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]]. Write $Du(t,x)$ for the total derivative in the spatial variable and $\operatorname{div}u=\operatorname{tr}(Du)$ ([[def-trace-of-a-square-matrix]]).

**(a) Incompressible Newtonian fluid.** Model data are a $C^1$ scalar field $p:I\times O\to\mathbb R$ (**pressure**) and a real number $\eta>0$ (**dynamic viscosity**; a dimensionless mathematical parameter until a unit system is fixed). The model consists of the **incompressibility constraint**

$$\operatorname{div}u(t,x)=0\qquad\bigl((t,x)\in I\times O\bigr)$$

and the **Newtonian stress field**

$$\sigma(t,x):=-p(t,x)I_3+\eta\bigl(Du(t,x)+Du(t,x)^{\mathsf T}\bigr)\in M_3(\mathbb R),$$

with $Du^{\mathsf T}$ the transpose and $I_3$ the identity ([[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]], [[def-matrix-space]]). The second term is symmetric, so $\sigma$ is symmetric for every $(t,x)$.

**(b) Barotropic inviscid fluid.** Model data are a $C^1$ function $p:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ (**pressure law**) and a $C^1$ **potential** $V:I\times O\to\mathbb R$. The **enthalpy** of the pressure law is the $C^1$ function

$$h(\rho):=\int_1^\rho\frac{p'(s)}{s}\,ds\qquad(\rho>0),$$

which is characterised by $h(1)=0$ and $h'(\rho)=p'(\rho)/\rho$ for every $\rho>0$ ([[def-the-integral-function]], [[thm-ftc-first-part]]). For a $C^1$ positive density field $\rho:I\times O\to(0,\infty)$ the branch's stress field is

$$\sigma(t,x):=-p\bigl(\rho(t,x)\bigr)I_3 ,$$

and the branch is **inviscid** (no velocity-gradient term) and **barotropic** (the stress depends on position and time only through the density).

items.title: Barotropic inviscid momentum in gradient form, Bernoulli along streamlines and the irrotational constant
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval and $O\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ open. Let $u:I\times O\to\mathbb R^3$ and $\rho:I\times O\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$, let $p:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$ with enthalpy $h(\rho_0)=\int_1^{\rho_0}p'(s)/s\,ds$, and let $V:I\times O\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$ ([[def-cm-fluid-constitutive-models]]). Write $\sigma:=-p(\rho)I_3$ and suppose that, on $I\times O$,

$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0 \qquad\text{and}\qquad \rho\,D_tu=\rho\,(-\nabla V)+g,\qquad g_i:=\sum_j\partial_j\sigma_{ij} . \tag{M}$$

(The local equation (M) is the conclusion of [[thm-cm-local-momentum-balance]] under its integral balance and continuity hypotheses; here it is the adopted local form of the barotropic inviscid model.)

**(i)** On $I\times O$,

$$D_tu=-\nabla\bigl(h(\rho)+V\bigr).$$

**(ii)** Suppose in addition that the flow is **steady**: $\partial_tu=0$, $\partial_t\rho=0$ and $\partial_tV=0$ on $I\times O$. A **streamline** on an open interval $J\subseteq I$ is a $C^1$ curve $\gamma:J\to O$ satisfying $\gamma'(t)=u(t,\gamma(t))$. For every streamline on a nonempty $J$,

$$\frac{d}{dt}\Bigl(h(\rho)+V+\tfrac12|u|_2^2\Bigr)\bigl(t,\gamma(t)\bigr)=0 ,$$

equivalently $u\cdot\nabla\bigl(h(\rho)+V+\tfrac12|u|_2^2\bigr)=0$ on $I\times O$: the quantity is constant along every streamline.

**(iii)** If the steady hypotheses of (ii) hold and in addition the spatial velocity gradient $Du(t,x)$ is symmetric at every $(t,x)$ (the **irrotational condition** used in this collection), then

$$\nabla\Bigl(h(\rho)+V+\tfrac12|u|_2^2\Bigr)=0\qquad\text{on }I\times O,$$

so the full derivative of this quantity vanishes and it is constant on every Euclidean ball contained in $I\times O$, hence on each connected component of $I\times O$.

items.title: Kelvin circulation: the circulation around a smooth material loop is constant in the barotropic inviscid model
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $u:I\times O\to\mathbb R^3$ and $\rho:I\times O\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$, let $p:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be the restriction of a $C^1$ map on an open neighbourhood of the rectangle, with enthalpy $h$, and let $V:I\times O\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, with the barotropic inviscid stress $\sigma=-p(\rho)I_3$; assume the local equations (M) of [[thm-cm-barotropic-momentum-and-bernoulli]] on $I\times O$:

$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0,\qquad \rho\,D_tu=\rho(-\nabla V)+g,\qquad g_i=\sum_j\partial_j\sigma_{ij},$$

so that, by part (i) of that theorem, $D_tu=-\nabla(h(\rho)+V)$ on $I\times O$.

Let $t_0<t_1$ with $[t_0,t_1]\subseteq I$ and let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\times[0,1]\to O$ be $C^1$ with

$$\gamma(t,0)=\gamma(t,1)\quad\text{and}\quad\partial_t\gamma(t,s)=u\bigl(t,\gamma(t,s)\bigr)\qquad\bigl((t,s)\in[t_0,t_1]\times[0,1]\bigr) .$$

Then the **circulation**

$$\Gamma(t):=\int_0^1\sum_{i=1}^3u_i\bigl(t,\gamma(t,s)\bigr)\,\partial_s\gamma_i(t,s)\,ds$$

is constant on $[t_0,t_1]$. The integral is an ordinary Riemann integral of a continuous real function; a singleton time interval has a trivially constant circulation and requires no time differentiation.

K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (September 1, 2026 complete volume), Section 8.4 (the Kelvin theorem for an ideal fluid)

items.title: d'Alembert's formula solves the wave equation, is the unique $C^2$ solution, and the fixed-end sine modes solve it exactly
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $c>0$.

**(a) The formula.** For every $f\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ and $g\in C^1(\mathbb R)$, the function

$$u(t,x):=\frac{f(x-ct)+f(x+ct)}{2}+\frac{1}{2c}\int_{x-ct}^{x+ct}g(s)\,ds \qquad\bigl((t,x)\in\mathbb R^2\bigr)$$

is of class $C^2$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) and satisfies

$$u_{tt}=c^2u_{xx},\qquad u(0,x)=f(x),\qquad u_t(0,x)=g(x)$$

for every $x\in\mathbb R$ ([[def-oriented-integral]], [[def-derivative]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If $u\in C^2(\mathbb R^2)$ satisfies $u_{tt}=c^2u_{xx}$ with $u(0,\cdot)=f$ and $u_t(0,\cdot)=g$ for $f\in C^2(\mathbb R)$, $g\in C^1(\mathbb R)$, then $u$ equals the formula in (a).

**(c) Fixed ends and modes.** Let $L>0$ and, for each integer $n\ge1$,

$$u_n(t,x):=\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr)\cos\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi ct}{L}\Bigr).$$

Then each $u_n$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^2$, satisfies $u_{tt}=c^2u_{xx}$, vanishes at $x=0$ and $x=L$ for every $t$, and has $u_n(0,x)=\sin(n\pi x/L)$, $\partial_tu_n(0,x)=0$. Every finite sum $\sum_{n\le N}\alpha_nu_n+\beta_n v_n$ with the companion modes $v_n(t,x):=\sin(n\pi x/L)\sin(n\pi ct/L)/(n\pi c/L)$ also solves the equation, vanishes at both ends and has the corresponding finite initial data.

references.title: J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (UC Davis), Chapter 7, Section 7.1 (the wave equation and the d'Alembert solution)
K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (September 1, 2026 complete volume), Sections 6.4–6.5 (the wave equation, its general traveling-wave solution and standing waves)

items.title: The cyclic spring chain, its discrete energy, and the smooth periodic comparison class
items.design_state: completed-local-definition; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $N\ge2$ be an integer, let $a>0$ and $c>0$ be real parameters, and let $L:=Na$. Indices are read modulo $N$: $z_{j+N}:=z_j$.

**(a) The chain.** A **state of the chain** is a pair $(q,p)\in\mathbb R^N\times\mathbb R^N$, where $q=(q_1,\dots,q_N)$ are the positions and $p=(q_1',\dots,q_N')$ the velocities of the $N$ nodes. The **cyclic spring-chain system** is the first-order system

$$q_j'=p_j,\qquad p_j'=\frac{c^2}{a^2}\bigl(q_{j+1}-2q_j+q_{j-1}\bigr)\qquad(j\in\mathbb Z/N),$$

equivalently the second-order system $q_j''=\frac{c^2}{a^2}(q_{j+1}-2q_j+q_{j-1})$ for a $C^2$ curve $q:I\to\mathbb R^N$. Its **discrete energy** is

$$E(q,p):=\frac12\sum_{j=1}^N\Bigl(p_j^2+\frac{c^2}{a^2}\bigl(q_{j+1}-q_j\bigr)^2\Bigr).$$

**(b) Discrete norms and differences.** For $z,w\in\mathbb R^N$ define the **scaled inner product and norm**

$$\langle z,w\rangle_a:=a\sum_{j=1}^N z_jw_j,\qquad \|z\|_a:=\langle z,z\rangle_a^{1/2},$$

and for the discrete difference $(D_+z)_j:=(z_{j+1}-z_j)/a$. The **discrete Laplacian** is $(\Delta_az)_j:=(z_{j+1}-2z_j+z_{j-1})/a^2$.

**(c) The comparison class.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval and let $u:I\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be a function that is $C^2$ in the first variable and $C^4$ in the second, is $L$-periodic in $x$ ($u(t,x+L)=u(t,x)$ for all $(t,x)$), and satisfies

$$u_{tt}(t,x)=c^2u_{xx}(t,x)\qquad\bigl((t,x)\in I\times\mathbb R\bigr).$$

For a compact subinterval $[0,T]\subseteq I$ put $M_T:=\sup\{|\partial_x^4u(t,x)|:(t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R\}$ (finite when continuous derivatives are bounded on the compact time interval, as assumed in the items that use it), and for $a=L/N$ define the **sampled initial data**

$$q_j(0):=u(0,ja),\qquad q_j'(0):=u_t(0,ja)\qquad(j=1,\dots,N).$$

items.title: Exact dispersion relation $\omega^2=(4c^2/a^2)\sin^2(\kappa a/2)$ for the cyclic chain and its continuum error bound
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $N\ge2$, $a>0$, $c>0$, let $\kappa,\omega\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\kappa Na\in2\pi\mathbb Z$, and let $A\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$. Consider the travelling cosine ansatz for the cyclic chain of [[def-cm-cyclic-spring-chain]]:

$$q_j(t):=A\cos(\kappa ja-\omega t)\qquad(j\in\mathbb Z/N).$$

**(a)** The curve $q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^N$ solves $q_j''=\frac{c^2}{a^2}(q_{j+1}-2q_j+q_{j-1})$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$ and all $j$ if and only if

$$\omega^2=\frac{4c^2}{a^2}\sin^2\!\Bigl(\frac{\kappa a}{2}\Bigr). \tag{DR}$$

**(b)** If (DR) holds and $|\kappa a|\le1$, then

$$\Bigl|\omega^2-c^2\kappa^2\Bigr|\le\frac{c^2\kappa^4a^2}{12},$$

so the continuum dispersion $\omega^2=c^2\kappa^2$ is recovered with an explicit fourth-order error in the spacing.

references.title: K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (September 1, 2026 complete volume), Section 6.3 (wave ansatz, dispersion relation (6.30) and the acoustic low-frequency limit)
I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014), Section 6.1 (the discrete chain and its continuum limit)

items.title: The centered second difference differs from the second derivative by at most $Ma^2/12$ when $|u''''|\le M$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval ([[def-interval]]), let $u:J\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^4$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), let $x\in J$ and $a>0$ satisfy $[x-a,x+a]\subseteq J$, and put

$$M:=\sup_{s\in[x-a,x+a]}|u''''(s)|<+\infty .$$

Then

$$\left|\frac{u(x+a)-2u(x)+u(x-a)}{a^2}-u''(x)\right|\le\frac{M\,a^2}{12}.$$

items.title: Discrete periodic summation by parts, the scaled Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, and the discrete energy identity
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Use the notation $z_{j+N}=z_j$, $(D_+z)_j=(z_{j+1}-z_j)/a$, $(\Delta_az)_j=(z_{j+1}-2z_j+z_{j-1})/a^2$, $\langle z,w\rangle_a=a\sum_jz_jw_j$, $\|z\|_a^2=\langle z,z\rangle_a$ and $E_a(q,p)=\tfrac12(\|p\|_a^2+c^2\|D_+q\|_a^2)$ of [[def-cm-cyclic-spring-chain]].

**(a) Summation by parts.** For all $z,w\in\mathbb R^N$,

$$\langle D_+z,D_+w\rangle_a=-\langle \Delta_az,w\rangle_a .$$

**(b) Scaled Cauchy-Schwarz.** For all $z,w\in\mathbb R^N$, $|\langle z,w\rangle_a|\le\|z\|_a\|w\|_a$ ([[prop-coordinate-cauchy-schwarz-agrees-with-the-finite-sum-theorem]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

**(c) Energy identity.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval, let $q:I\to\mathbb R^N$ be $C^2$ and let $R:I\to\mathbb R^N$ be continuous with

$$q_j''=\frac{c^2}{a^2}\bigl(q_{j+1}-2q_j+q_{j-1}\bigr)+R_j=c^2(\Delta_aq)_j+R_j\qquad(j\in\mathbb Z/N).$$

Then $t\mapsto E_a(q(t),q'(t))$ is $C^1$ on $I$ with

$$\frac{d}{dt}E_a\bigl(q(t),q'(t)\bigr)=a\sum_{j=1}^N R_j(t)\,q_j'(t),$$

and consequently $\bigl|\frac{d}{dt}E_a\bigr|\le\|R(t)\|_a\,\sqrt{2E_a(t)}$ whenever $E_a\ge0$ (which always holds).

references.title: I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014), Section 6.1 (the quadratic chain energy (6.1))

G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems (AMS Graduate Studies in Mathematics 140, online edition), Problem 5.5 (harmonic crystal in one dimension) and the nearest-neighbour lattice example (8.81) in Section 8.4

items.title: Finite-time continuum limit of the cyclic spring chain: uniform $O(a^{3/2})$ nodal and uniform interpolation convergence
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $L>0$, $c>0$, let $N\ge2$ be an integer and $a:=L/N$, and let $[0,T]$ be a compact time interval, with $T\ge0$. Let

$$u:[0,T]\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$$

be $C^2$ in $t$ and $C^4$ in $x$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), $L$-periodic in $x$, and satisfy $u_{tt}=c^2u_{xx}$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R$; put

$$M:=\sup_{[0,T]\times\mathbb R}|\partial_x^4u|<+\infty,\qquad M_2:=\sup_{[0,T]\times\mathbb R}|\partial_x^2u|<+\infty .$$

Let $q:[0,T]\to\mathbb R^N$ be the (by (i), unique) solution of the cyclic spring-chain system of [[def-cm-cyclic-spring-chain]] with the sampled initial data $q_j(0)=u(0,ja)$, $q_j'(0)=u_t(0,ja)$, and put

$$e_j(t):=q_j(t)-u(t,ja),\qquad C:=\frac{c^2\sqrt L\,M}{12}.$$

Then:

Here smoothness on the closed time interval means restriction of a map defined on an open neighbourhood, with the indicated derivatives extending continuously to the interval. A chain solution on $[0,T]$ is the restriction of a solution on an open time interval containing $[0,T]$; the sampled derivative $q_j\prime(0)$ is the derivative of that solution. Thus derivatives remain defined when $T=0$. Uniqueness concerns the restricted state $(q,q\prime)$.

**(i)** the solution $q$ exists and is unique on $[0,T]$;

**(ii)** for every $t\in[0,T]$,

$$\|e(t)\|_a\le\frac{Ca^2t^2}{2},\qquad \|e'(t)\|_a\le Ca^2t ;$$

**(iii)** consequently $\max_j|e_j(t)|\le \tfrac12Ca^{3/2}t^2$ for $t\in[0,T]$, so the nodal error tends to $0$ uniformly as $a\to0$;

**(iv)** let $I_aq(t,\cdot)$ be the piecewise-linear function on $[0,L]$ that equals $q_j(t)$ at $x=ja$ and is extended $L$-periodically; then for the periodic extension of $u$,

$$\sup_{x\in[0,L]}\bigl|I_aq(t,x)-u(t,x)\bigr|\le\max_j|e_j(t)|+\frac{M_2a^2}{8}\qquad(0\le t\le T),$$

so the interpolated chain displacement converges to $u$ uniformly on $[0,T]\times[0,L]$ as $a\to0$.

references.title: I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014), Section 6.1 (the chain-to-continuum limit, Eqs. (6.1)–(6.8))

G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems (AMS Graduate Studies in Mathematics 140, online edition), Problem 5.5 (harmonic crystal in one dimension) and the nearest-neighbour lattice example (8.81) in Section 8.4

items.title: The method of characteristics for $u_t+uu_x=0$ and the finite blow-up time of the gradient
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $f\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) be bounded (so $\|f\|_\infty<+\infty$, [[thm-extreme-value-metric]], [[thm-heine-borel-rn]]) and suppose that

$$f'(a)\ge -K\quad\text{for every }a\in\mathbb R,\qquad\text{and}\qquad f'(a_*)=-K\ \text{for some }a_*\in\mathbb R,$$

with $K>0$. Put $T_0:=1/K$, and for $0\le t<T_0$ define $\varphi_t(a):=a+t f(a)$.

**(i)** For every $t\in[0,T_0)$ the map $\varphi_t:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism onto $\mathbb R$ ([[cor-injective-regular-ck-map-is-a-ck-diffeomorphism-onto-its-image]]), and with $a(t,x):=\varphi_t^{-1}(x)$ the **characteristic label**,

$$u(t,x):=f\bigl(a(t,x)\bigr),\qquad (t,x)\in[0,T_0)\times\mathbb R,$$

is $C^1$ jointly in $(t,x)$, satisfies $u(0,x)=f(x)$ and solves Burgers' equation

$$u_t(t,x)+u(t,x)\,u_x(t,x)=0\qquad\text{on }(0,T_0)\times\mathbb R . \tag{B}$$

**(ii)** For every $a_0\in\mathbb R$ the function $t\mapsto u(t,\varphi_t(a_0))=f(a_0)$ is constant, and the gradient along this characteristic, $q(t):=u_x(t,\varphi_t(a_0))$, satisfies $q'=-q^2$ and $q(t)=f'(a_0)/(1+tf'(a_0))$ for $0\le t<T_0$.

**(iii)** Put $x_*:=\varphi_{T_0}(a_*)=a_*+T_0f(a_*)$ and let $a(t):=a(t,x_*)$ for $0\le t<T_0$. The level set $S:=\{a:\varphi_{T_0}(a)=x_*\}$ is a nonempty compact interval $[\alpha,\beta]$. Put $a^\dagger:=\min\{\max\{x_*,\alpha\},\beta\}$. Then $a(t)\to a^\dagger$ (in particular $a(t)\to a_*$ when $S=\{a_*\}$), $f'(a(t))\to-K$, and

$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|u_x(t,x)|\ \ge\ |u_x(t,x_*)|\ =\ \frac{|f'(a(t))|}{1+t\,f'(a(t))}\ \longrightarrow\ +\infty\qquad(t\uparrow T_0),$$

while $|u(t,x_*)|=|f(a(t))|\le\|f\|_\infty$ stays bounded. Thus the smooth solution obtained by characteristics has a gradient blow-up at the finite time $T_0$ although the solution values and the characteristic locations remain finite; $C^1$ solvability up to time $T_0$ is not asserted.

items.title: Weak and entropy solutions of the scalar conservation law $u_t+(u^2/2)_x=0$
items.design_state: completed-local-definition; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the actual Lebesgue measure foundation used by the bounded Borel weak/entropy class.

Write $F(u):=\tfrac12u^2$ and let $\lambda_2$ be two-dimensional Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^2$ ([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]).

Every space-time expression written as $\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_{\mathbb R}(\cdots)\,dx\,dt$ below means the single signed Lebesgue integral over $[0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ with respect to $\lambda_2$; it is not an iterated-integral convention. The initial-data integral is with respect to one-dimensional Lebesgue measure $\lambda_1$. In (W) and (E), each integrand is Borel measurable, bounded, and supported in the compact support of the test function (or its initial trace). A compact support is contained in a bounded rectangle of finite Lebesgue measure, by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]]; monotonicity and homogeneity of the nonnegative integral give $\int |q|\le\|q\|_\infty\lambda_d(K)<\infty$ for such an integrand $q$ supported in $K$ ([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). Thus all displayed signed integrals are defined as Lebesgue integrals of integrable functions ([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]).

A **test function** is a function $\varphi:[0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^1$ up to the boundary: it is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open neighborhood of this closed half-space, and its support within the half-space is compact. No vanishing or continuation by zero for $t<0$ is required. Thus the trace $\varphi(0,x)$ may be nonzero. Derivatives at $t=0$ are the continuous one-sided derivatives. Write $C_c^1([0,\infty)\times\mathbb R)$ for this class; **admissible** means belonging to this class and **nonnegative** means $\varphi\ge0$ on the half-space.

**(a) Weak solutions.** Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be bounded and Borel measurable ([[def-extended-real-valued-measurable-function]]) and let $u:(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be bounded and Borel measurable. Then $u$ is a **weak solution of**

$$u_t+\bigl(F(u)\bigr)_x=0 \qquad\text{with }u(0,\cdot)=f \tag{CL}$$

when

$$\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_{\mathbb R}\Bigl[u(t,x)\varphi_t(t,x)+F\bigl(u(t,x)\bigr)\varphi_x(t,x)\Bigr]dx\,dt+\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)\varphi(0,x)\,dx=0 \tag{W}$$

for every test function $\varphi$ ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]). The integrals exist because $u,f$ are bounded and the test functions have compact support; the identity depends on $u$ and $f$ only through their almost-everywhere classes.

**(b) Entropy pairs.** An **entropy pair** is a pair $(\eta,q)$ of $C^1$ functions $\eta,q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-derivative]]) such that

$$q'(u)=\eta'(u)\,F'(u)=u\,\eta'(u)\qquad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb R;$$

the function $\eta$ is then called an **entropy** and $q$ its **entropy flux**. The entropy is **convex** when $\eta((1-a)r+as)\le(1-a)\eta(r)+a\eta(s)$ for all real $r,s$ and $a\in[0,1]$.

**(c) Entropy solutions.** A weak solution $u$ of (CL) is an **entropy solution** when, for every convex entropy pair $(\eta,q)$ with $q'=u\eta'$, the distributional inequality

$$\bigl(\eta(u)\bigr)_t+\bigl(q(u)\bigr)_x\le0$$

holds, by definition meaning that

$$\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_{\mathbb R}\Bigl[\eta\bigl(u\bigr)\varphi_t+q\bigl(u\bigr)\varphi_x\Bigr]dx\,dt+\int_{\mathbb R}\eta\bigl(f(x)\bigr)\varphi(0,x)\,dx\ \ge\ 0 \tag{E}$$

for every nonnegative test function $\varphi$.

**(d) Riemann data.** For reals $u_L,u_R$ the **Riemann initial data** are

$$f(x):=\begin{cases}u_L,&x<0,\\ u_R,&x\ge0.\end{cases}$$

items.title: Riemann shock and rarefaction waves for $u_t+(u^2/2)_x=0$ are weak solutions, and the shock is an entropy solution
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Lebesgue weak formulation and the imported divergence theorem.

Let $F(u)=\tfrac12u^2$ and use the weak and entropy formulations of [[def-cm-scalar-conservation-law-weak-and-entropy-solution]].

**(a) Shock.** Let $u_L>u_R$, put $s:=(u_L+u_R)/2$ and

$$u(t,x):=\begin{cases}u_L,&x<st,\\ u_R,&x\ge st,\end{cases}\qquad(t>0),$$

with Riemann initial data $f$ equal to $u_L$ for $x<0$ and $u_R$ for $x\ge0$. Values on the shock line or at the single initial jump point do not change the integral identities. Then $u$ is a weak solution of $u_t+(F(u))_x=0$ with initial data $f$.

**(b) Entropy of the shock.** For every $k\in\mathbb R$, set $\eta_k(u):=|u-k|$ and $q_k(u):=\operatorname{sgn}(u-k)\,(u^2-k^2)/2$ for $u\ne k$, with $q_k(k):=0$. Then the entropy inequality (E) of [[def-cm-scalar-conservation-law-weak-and-entropy-solution]] holds for the pair $(\eta_k,q_k)$, with interface coefficient

$$s\,[\eta_k]-[q_k]=\begin{cases}-(k-u_L)(k-u_R),&u_R\le k\le u_L,\\0,&k\notin[u_R,u_L],\end{cases}\quad\ge0 ,$$

where $[h]:=h(u_R)-h(u_L)$. The shock also satisfies (E) for every convex $C^1$ entropy pair of the Definition, and is an entropy solution in its full declared sense.

**(c) Rarefaction.** Let $u_L<u_R$ and define

$$u(t,x):=\begin{cases}u_L,&x\le u_Lt,\\ x/t,&u_Lt<x<u_Rt,\\ u_R,&x\ge u_Rt,\end{cases}\qquad(t>0).$$

Then $u$ is continuous on $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, is a weak solution of $u_t+(F(u))_x=0$ with the Riemann initial data, and satisfies the entropy inequality (E) for every convex $C^1$ entropy pair and for every pair $(\eta_k,q_k)$, $k\in\mathbb R$ (indeed with equality), and is an entropy solution.

items.title: Exact plane Poiseuille and Couette flows of the incompressible Newtonian model, with flux and ansatz uniqueness
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
The flux integrals below are ordinary Riemann integrals of continuous profiles on $[0,h]$.

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open time interval, let $\rho>0$, $\eta>0$ and $h>0$ be constants, and let $O:=\mathbb R\times(0,h)\times\mathbb R$ with spatial coordinates $(x,y,z)$. Let $v\in C([0,h])\cap C^2((0,h))$, with endpoint values given by its continuous extension, and $p_{\rm sp}\in C^1(O)$. Define stationary spacetime fields $u:I\times O\to\mathbb R^3$ and $p:I\times O\to\mathbb R$ by $u(t,x,y,z):=(v(y),0,0)$ and $p(t,x,y,z):=p_{\rm sp}(x,y,z)$. Here $D_xu$ denotes the spatial total derivative at fixed $t$, $(u\cdot\nabla)u:=D_xu\,u$, and $\Delta u:=(\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_j^2u_i)_{i=1}^3$ acts componentwise ([[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]]). The incompressible Newtonian equations of [[def-cm-fluid-constitutive-models]] with no body force and steady data read

$$\operatorname{div}u=0,\qquad \rho\,(u\cdot\nabla)u=-\nabla p+\eta\,\Delta u , \tag{NS}$$

where the second equation is the adopted stationary momentum equation with $\sigma=-pI_3+\eta(D_xu+(D_xu)^{\mathsf T})$.

For this item, “irrotational” means that the spatial velocity gradient $D_xu$ is symmetric.

**(a) Plane Poiseuille flow.** Let $G\in\mathbb R$, $p_0\in\mathbb R$ and

$$v(y):=\frac{G\,y(h-y)}{2\eta},\qquad p_{\rm sp}(x,y,z):=p_0-Gx.$$

Then $u$ is $C^\infty$ on $I\times O$, satisfies (NS) there, and $v(0)=v(h)=0$. Its flux per unit width is

$$\int_0^hv(y)\,dy=\frac{Gh^3}{12\eta}.$$

Moreover, within the ansatz $u=(v(y),0,0)$, $p=p_0-Gx$ with the same constant $G$ and the no-slip conditions $v(0)=v(h)=0$, this is the only solution: any two such profiles differ by a linear function vanishing at both endpoints, hence coincide.

**(b) Plane Couette flow.** Let $V\in\mathbb R$, let $v(y):=Vy/h$, and let $p_{\rm sp}$ be constant. Then the stationary $u,p$ defined above satisfy (NS) on $I\times O$ and $v(0)=0$, $v(h)=V$. If $V\ne0$, the velocity gradient $D_xu$ is not symmetric, so the flow is not irrotational by the definition above.

items.title: Sine coefficients, sine series and the odd periodic extension
items.design_state: completed-local-definition; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $L>0$. A function $F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is **$L$-periodic** when $F(x+L)=F(x)$ for all $x\in\mathbb R$, and **odd** when $F(-x)=-F(x)$ for all $x$.

**(a) Sine coefficients.** Let $F:[0,L]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]); a function on a larger domain is used through its restriction to $[0,L]$, with no periodicity required for the coefficient definition. In particular both $L$-periodic and odd $2L$-periodic functions are admissible. Then $\int_0^L|F|<\infty$ ([[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]). For every integer $n\ge1$ the **$n$-th sine coefficient** of $F$ is

$$b_n(F):=\frac{2}{L}\int_0^LF(x)\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr)dx \qquad \in\mathbb R ,$$

an ordinary Riemann integral of a continuous function on a compact interval ([[def-oriented-integral]], [[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]]). The **sine series** of $F$ is the series of functions

$$\sum_{n\ge1}b_n(F)\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr),$$

whose $N$-th **partial sum** is $S_N^{\rm s}F(x):=\sum_{n\le N}b_n(F)\sin(n\pi x/L)$.

**(b) Odd periodic extension.** Let $F:[0,L]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous with $F(0)=F(L)=0$. The **odd $2L$-periodic extension** of $F$ is the function on $\mathbb R$ defined by

$$F^{\rm odd}(x):=\begin{cases}F(x),&0\le x\le L,\\ -F(-x),&-L\le x\le 0,\end{cases}\qquad F^{\rm odd}(x+2L):=F^{\rm odd}(x).$$

Equivalently, $F^{\rm odd}$ is the unique $2L$-periodic odd function whose restriction to $[0,L]$ is $F$ (the two definitions agree at $0$ and $L$ because both values vanish; the extension is well defined and continuous).

(c) Given a specified wave speed $c>0$, the **angular frequency** of mode $n$ is $\omega_n:=cn\pi/L$; its fundamental ($n=1$) value is $c\pi/L$.

items.title: Sine orthogonality on a half period and the full-period integrals of odd $2L$-periodic functions
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
All integrals in this statement and proof are ordinary Riemann integrals of continuous functions on compact intervals, as in [[def-cm-sine-coefficients-of-periodic-functions]].

Let $L>0$. Then:

**(a)** For all integers $n,k\ge1$,

$$\int_0^L\sin\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr)\sin\Bigl(\frac{k\pi x}{L}\Bigr)dx=\frac{L}{2}\,\delta_{nk}.$$

**(b)** Let $W:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]), odd and $2L$-periodic. Then

$$\int_0^{2L}W(x)\,dx=0,\qquad \int_0^{2L}W(x)\cos\Bigl(\frac{k\pi x}{L}\Bigr)dx=0\quad\text{for every integer }k ,$$

and, for every integer $k\ge1$,

$$\frac{1}{2L}\int_0^{2L}W(x)\sin\Bigl(\frac{k\pi x}{L}\Bigr)dx=\frac{1}{L}\int_0^{L}W(x)\sin\Bigl(\frac{k\pi x}{L}\Bigr)dx .$$

items.title: Fejer completeness: a continuous one-periodic function with all integrals against the characters vanishing is zero
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be one-periodic, meaning $h(t+1)=h(t)$ for all real $t$, and continuous, meaning that both real functions $\operatorname{Re}h,\operatorname{Im}h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy [[def-continuity-real]] and suppose that

$$\int_0^1h(t)\,e_k(-t)\,dt=0\qquad\text{for every }k\in\mathbb Z,$$

All integrals here are componentwise Riemann integrals: for continuous $p=p_1+ip_2$, $\int_a^b p:=\int_a^b p_1+i\int_a^b p_2$, with the real oriented convention of [[def-oriented-integral]]; both integrals exist by [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]. Here $e_k(t):=e^{2\pi ikt}$ ([[def-complex-exponential]]). Then $h=0$ on $\mathbb R$.

items.title: Uniform convergence of a $C^2$ sequence with its first and second derivatives on a rectangle passes $C^2$ regularity and termwise differentiation to the limit
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $T,L>0$ and $R:=[0,T]\times[0,L]$ ([[def-interval]]). For each $k\in\mathbb N$ let $u_k$ be of class $C^2$ on an open neighbourhood of $R$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Suppose that on $R$:

$$u_k\to u,\quad \partial_tu_k\to v,\quad \partial_xu_k\to w,\quad \partial_t^2u_k\to v_2,\quad \partial_t\partial_xu_k\to z,\quad \partial_x^2u_k\to w_2$$

pointwise for $u$ and uniformly for the five derivative sequences ([[def-continuity-real]]). Then $u$ is $C^2$ on the interior of $R$, all listed limits are continuous on $R$, and on the interior

$$\partial_tu=v,\quad \partial_xu=w,\quad \partial_t^2u=v_2,\quad \partial_t\partial_xu=\partial_x\partial_tu=z,\quad \partial_x^2u=w_2 ,$$

the derivatives extending continuously to $R$.

items.title: Repeated integration by parts gives $|b_n(F)|\le 2L^5M_5/(\pi^5n^5)$ for odd $2L$-periodic $C^5$ functions and $|b_n(G)|\le 2L^4M_4/(\pi^4n^4)$ for $C^4$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $L>0$. Let $F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be odd and $2L$-periodic of class $C^5$ and let $G:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be odd and $2L$-periodic of class $C^4$ ([[def-cm-sine-coefficients-of-periodic-functions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); put

$$M_5:=\sup_{\mathbb R}|F^{(5)}|<+\infty,\qquad M_4:=\sup_{\mathbb R}|G^{(4)}|<+\infty .$$

Then for every integer $n\ge1$, with the sine coefficients $b_n$ of [[def-cm-sine-coefficients-of-periodic-functions]],

$$|b_n(F)|\le\frac{2L^5M_5}{\pi^5n^5},\qquad |b_n(G)|\le\frac{2L^4M_4}{\pi^4n^4}.$$

L. Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, 3rd ed., Section 3.3.2 (decay of Fourier coefficients of smooth functions)

items.title: The smooth fixed-end string: the sine series solves the wave equation with the given data, uniquely, with an explicit tail bound
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $L>0$, $c>0$. Let $F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be odd and $2L$-periodic of class $C^5$ and let $G:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be odd and $2L$-periodic of class $C^4$ ([[def-cm-sine-coefficients-of-periodic-functions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), with $M_5:=\sup|F^{(5)}|<\infty$, $M_4:=\sup|G^{(4)}|<\infty$. Put

$$a_n:=b_n(F),\qquad d_n:=\frac{b_n(G)}{\omega_n},\qquad \omega_n:=\frac{cn\pi}{L}\qquad(n\ge1),$$

and define, for $(t,x)\in\mathbb R^2$,

$$u(t,x):=\sum_{n\ge1}\Bigl[a_n\cos(\omega_nt)+d_n\sin(\omega_nt)\Bigr]\sin\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr). \tag{S}$$

Then:

**(i)** the series (S) and the termwise series of $\partial_tu,\partial_xu,\partial_t^2u,\partial_t\partial_xu,\partial_x^2u$ converge absolutely and uniformly on every strip $[-T,T]\times[0,L]$; the sum $u$ is $C^2$, is odd and $2L$-periodic in $x$, satisfies $u_{tt}=c^2u_{xx}$, obeys the fixed-end conditions $u(t,0)=u(t,L)=0$, and has

$$u(0,x)=F(x),\qquad u_t(0,x)=G(x)\qquad(x\in\mathbb R).$$

**(ii)** (Uniqueness.) If $v$ is $C^2$ on $[0,T]\times[0,L]$ for some $T>0$, satisfies $v_{tt}=c^2v_{xx}$ there, $v(t,0)=v(t,L)=0$ for all $t$, and $v(0,\cdot)=v_t(0,\cdot)=0$, then $v=0$ on $[0,T]\times[0,L]$.

**(iii)** (Tail bound.) For every $N\ge1$ and every $(t,x)\in[-T,T]\times[0,L]$,

$$\Bigl|u(t,x)-\sum_{n\le N}\Bigl[a_n\cos(\omega_nt)+d_n\sin(\omega_nt)\Bigr]\sin\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr)\Bigr|\le C\,(N+1)^{-4},$$

where $C:=2\bigl(\frac{2L^5M_5}{\pi^5}+\frac{2L^5M_4}{c\pi^5}\bigr)$.

references.title: R. Laugesen, Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes (arXiv:0903.3845), Chapters 1–2 (Fourier coefficients, summability and the uniqueness theorem (2.14))
K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (September 1, 2026 complete volume), Section 6.5 (standing waves of the fixed-end string)

items.title: Transport of a translating rigid region: the rate integral vanishes for a travelling profile
items.reference: batch-8 B page; constructed from the A-page statements
items.design_state: completed-local-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the actual Lebesgue transport and change-of-variables suppliers.

Let $B:=B_1(0)\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be the open unit ball ([[def-metric-ball]]), a nonempty bounded open set and hence a material region in the sense of [[def-cm-material-region-and-density]]; let $v\in\mathbb R^3$ be fixed, and let

$$\psi(t,X):=X+tv\qquad(t\in\mathbb R,\ X\in\mathbb R^3)$$

be the uniform translation motion of [[def-cm-continuum-motion]] (each $\psi_t$ is the identity plus a translation, a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism with $D_X\psi_t=I_3$). Let $h:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) and define the travelling profile

$$f(t,x):=h(x-tv)\qquad\bigl((t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\bigr).$$

Then $\int_{\psi_t(B)}f(t,x)\,dx$ is independent of $t$, while the transport integrand vanishes pointwise:

$$\partial_tf+\operatorname{div}(fv)=0,$$

so the transport theorem reproduces the constant rate $0$.

references.title: R. Abeyaratne, Continuum Mechanics, Volume II of Lecture Notes on the Mechanics of Solids (MIT, 1988, revised 2020), Sections 3.7, 4.2 and 4.4 (transport equations; mass and momentum balance in integral form)

items.title: A longitudinal plane wave in the isotropic elastic model: dispersion check and strain energy at explicit parameters
items.reference: batch-8 B page; constructed from the A-page statements
items.design_state: completed-local-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Take $\lambda=2$, $\mu=1$, $\rho_0=1$ ([[def-cm-linear-elastic-constitutive-law]]: here $\lambda+\frac{2\mu}{3}=\frac83>0$). Let $k=(\pi,0,0)$, $a=(1,0,0)$ and

$$\xi(t,x)=a\cos(\pi x_1-\omega t),\qquad \omega:=2\pi .$$

Then $\xi$ is a longitudinal plane wave with speed $\sqrt{(\lambda+2\mu)/\rho_0}=2$, and the associated strain and stress satisfy the elastic momentum identity; the strain energy density at time $t$ equals both $W(e)=2\pi^2\sin^2(\pi x_1-\omega t)$ and the decomposition $\mu|e_0|_F^2+(\lambda/2+\mu/3)(\operatorname{tr}e)^2$ with the same value.

items.title: The first sine mode with matched velocity data: exact solution and the numerical tail bound $8(N+1)^{-4}$
items.reference: batch-8 B page; constructed from the A-page statements
items.design_state: completed-local-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $L>0$, $c>0$ and define the odd $2L$-periodic $C^\infty$ datum

$$F(x):=\sin\Bigl(\frac{\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\qquad G(x):=\frac{c\pi}{L}\sin\Bigl(\frac{\pi x}{L}\Bigr).$$

Then the sine coefficients of [the definition] are $b_1(F)=1$ and $b_n(F)=0$ for $n\ge2$, and $b_1(G)=c\pi/L$, $b_n(G)=0$ for $n\ge2$; the series solution of the string theorem is the finite expression

$$u(t,x)=\bigl[\cos(\omega_1t)+\sin(\omega_1t)\bigr]\sin\Bigl(\frac{\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\qquad \omega_1=\frac{c\pi}{L},$$

which solves $u_{tt}=c^2u_{xx}$ with $u(0,\cdot)=F$, $u_t(0,\cdot)=G$ and $u(t,0)=u(t,L)=0$; its tail beyond the first mode vanishes, and the numerical bound of the string theorem at these data is

$$|u(t,x)-u_1(t,x)|\le 8\,(N+1)^{-4}\qquad(N\ge2),$$

so the general bound is valid but far from sharp on this datum.

references.title: K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (September 1, 2026 complete volume), Section 6.5 (standing waves of the fixed-end string)
R. Laugesen, Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes (arXiv:0903.3845), Chapters 1–2 (Fourier coefficients and summability)

items.title: FALSE: the $O(N^{-4})$ sine-tail bound holds for every continuous odd periodic function. A $C^1$ datum with coefficients $n^{-3}$ refutes it

items.statement:
**False statement.** For every continuous odd $2L$-periodic function $F$ there is a constant $C_F$ such that, for every $N\ge1$,

$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\Bigl|F(x)-S_N^{\rm s}F(x)\Bigr|\le C_F\,(N+1)^{-4},$$

where $S_N^{\rm s}F$ is the $N$-th partial sum of the sine series of [[def-cm-sine-coefficients-of-periodic-functions]].

(The theorem of this collection proves the bound only under the $C^5$ hypothesis of [[thm-cm-smooth-string-fourier-series-solution]]; the statement above drops that hypothesis, and that is exactly what fails.)

references.title: R. Laugesen, Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes (arXiv:0903.3845), Chapters 1 and 5 (smoothness and decay of Fourier coefficients; Fourier series in L²(T))

items.title: Numerical checks for channel flows: $h=\eta=1$, $G=12$ gives flux $1$ and centre speed $3/2$, and $V=2$ gives shear $2$
items.reference: batch-8 B page; constructed from the A-page statements
items.design_state: completed-local-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Take $h=1$, $\eta=1$ in the plane channel of [[thm-cm-plane-couette-and-poiseuille-flows]].

1. **Poiseuille, $G=12$.** The profile is $v(y)=6y(1-y)$; its flux per unit width is $1$ and its maximal speed is $v(1/2)=3/2$.

2. **Couette, $V=2$.** The profile is $v(y)=2y$; the only nonzero entry of $Du$ is $\partial_yu_1=2$, so the antisymmetric part of the velocity gradient has magnitude $1$ in the relevant off-diagonal slots and the flow is not irrotational.

references.title: K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (September 1, 2026 complete volume), Section 8.5 (the Couette and Poiseuille channel-flow examples and the discharge law)

items.title: A four-node cyclic chain mode with $a=c=1$: exact ODE check, dispersion value $\omega^2=2$, and the continuum error bound
items.reference: batch-8 B page; constructed from the A-page statements
items.design_state: completed-local-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Take $N=4$, $a=1$, $c=1$ in the cyclic chain of [[def-cm-cyclic-spring-chain]]. The wave number $\kappa=\pi/2$ gives

$$\omega^2=\frac{4c^2}{a^2}\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{\kappa a}{2}\Bigr)=4\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{4}\Bigr)=2,\qquad \omega=\sqrt2,$$

and the profile $q_j(t)=\cos\bigl(\frac{\pi j}{2}-\sqrt2\,t\bigr)$, $j\in\mathbb Z/4$, solves the chain equation exactly; the continuum comparison at this wave number gives the exact error $|\omega^2-c^2\kappa^2|=\frac{\pi^2}{4}-2$ against the exact bound $\frac{c^2\kappa^4a^2}{12}=\frac{\pi^4}{192}$.

references.title: K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (September 1, 2026 complete volume), Section 6.3 (chain modes, dispersion relation and the continuum limit)
I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014), Section 6.1 (the discrete chain and its continuum limit)
